title: Normal Calibration of Horvitz-Thompson Effects in Binary Finite Populations under Delocalized Dependence
banked_reason: Terminal kernel substitution: the promised sharp every-sequence iff frontier, exact modulus and universal converses remain open; the delivered sound sufficient-region/H3-obstruction bracket is a strictly weaker kernel. Independent validity gate confirmed no concrete faithful untried route.
gap_reasons: The promised sharp every-sequence iff frontier with a modulus exact on that region and converses for every excluded subsequence is still posed as open; the delivered sufficient-region/H3-obstruction bracket is a strictly weaker kernel.

Position the actual bracket theorem at theorem level against the closest GDO local-operator result and nonstationary Gaussian-array result, stating precisely what this sufficient certificate and single obstruction add rather than only listing donor limitations.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived an informally audited sufficient calibration certificate, a restricted H3 obstruction, and fixed-cap inference, with all six cited leaves verified from lawful primary-source excerpts. The exact every-sequence frontier, an exact public modulus, full-sign replacement on the ell^2/n branch, and universal converse remained open; independent validity review confirmed failure to deliver the accepted kernel. Formalization did not start, and the original frontier is not refuted; sound partial work is retained for a separately reviewed future proposal.
tldr: The contribution is an explicit uniform sufficient certificate for oracle normal calibration of the fixed binary finite-population HT ATE, together with a legal H3 obstruction; the exact joint spectrum and coherence frontier remains open. The certificate retains every matrix and bounded labeled schedule in the maintained class. Its proved regimes include vanishing \(\delta_n^2\ell_n\), a fixed effective cap, \(\ell_n^3/n\to0\), and the independent cases \(\delta_n=0\) or \(L_n=1\). The H3 diagnostic excludes its specified actual-cap subsequences. Conservative assigned-record intervals of bounded relative width are supplied only on fixed spectral caps. Oracle normality and feasible scale information remain distinct.
gap: Inspected local-coupling and ordered-array results do not characterize uniform full-sign calibration on the entire joint matrix envelope. A fixed-chaos theorem does not justify replacement of high-order variance.
fill: The kernel derives \(\Gamma_v\), \(R_v\), and legal non-Gaussian arrays for every excluded sequence. Fixed-cap intervals and exact covariance certificates support the consumer; pair-HT refinement does not replace the frontier.
